first.rationale: Onboarding deterioration is directly observable, and simplification has prior evidence of improving completion and adoption. Verify that result’s connection to qualified revenue, while also checking promotional pricing for retention, discount dependency, and customer-quality effects before rejecting it despite the competitive threat. Current intent favors a guarded onboarding test because pricing carries greater downstream-value risk under a sustainable long-term revenue objective.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source shows materially higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle: although it lifted signup and qualified revenue initially, the verified cohort suffered 12% lower retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Proceed with shortened onboarding despite the competitor’s deeper price cut. Verified evidence shows gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not answer the churn pressure with broad promotional pricing: the verified 40% discount cohort had 12% lower retention and failed at first renewal. The doubled churn conversations raise urgency but do not overturn that observed downstream-value risk; pricing-specific retention alternatives remain unverified until next cycle.
